title: Gosari Namul Seasoned Fernbrake
shortDescription: Commercially processed, fully softened fernbrake is re-blanched, seasoned with soy and perilla oil, and stir-fried until tender.
culturalContext: Gosari namul is a Korean seasoned fernbrake side dish and a common bibimbap component. This conservative draft uses only commercially processed, fully softened gosari and does not instruct foraging or raw-bracken processing.
author: {{LEGAL_NAME}}

ingredients.preparation: label states ready for cooking; drained

instructions.heading: Verify the product
instructions.action: Use only sealed, commercially processed gosari whose label confirms it is fully softened and ready for cooking; follow any stricter directions.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: The product identity and preparation state are confirmed.
instructions.safetyNote: Do not forage, identify, or process raw or dried bracken using this draft.

instructions.heading: Re-blanch
instructions.action: Bring water to a full boil, add the prepared gosari for 30 seconds, then drain.
instructions.safetyNote: Open the pot away from your face and avoid steam burns.

instructions.heading: Cut and season
instructions.action: Cool just enough to handle, cut into bite-size lengths, and mix with soy sauce and perilla oil.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Stems are evenly seasoned and remain intact.
instructions.safetyNote: Use clean utensils and verify soy sauce allergens.

instructions.heading: Stir-fry
instructions.action: Heat neutral oil over medium, add gosari, and stir gently until hot and most moisture evaporates.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Stems are tender and the pan is nearly dry.
instructions.safetyNote: Follow any package heating direction if it is stricter.

instructions.heading: Finish
instructions.action: Remove from heat and mix in sesame oil and ground sesame seeds.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: The seasoning coats evenly without pooled liquid.
instructions.safetyNote: Declare soy, wheat/gluten, and sesame allergens.

instructions.heading: Serve or chill
instructions.action: Transfer to a clean dish, rest 5 minutes, and serve warm or cool.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: The stems are tender but not disintegrating.

grillSetup: Not applicable; this banchan is prepared on the stovetop or as a seasoned side.
targetInternalTemperature: Follow the commercially processed gosari package directions; re-blanch and stir-fry until steaming throughout.
foodSafetyNotes: Use only commercially processed, fully softened, correctly identified gosari.
Do not forage or use this draft to process raw or dried bracken.
Follow the package preparation, heating, and storage directions.
Refrigerate within 2 hours at or below 40°F / 4°C.

allergens.crossContactWarning: Contains soy, wheat/gluten, and sesame; verify every label.

substitutions: Do not substitute wild, fresh, or unidentified fern material.
Use certified gluten-free tamari only after verifying the label.
ingredientSourcing: Buy sealed prepared gosari from a reputable Korean market and retain the original label.
makeAhead: Prepare up to 1 day ahead, cool promptly, cover, and refrigerate.
storage: Follow the package direction; absent a stricter instruction, refrigerate within 2 hours and use within 3 days pending qualified review.
reheating: Reheat until steaming throughout or serve properly refrigerated portions cool.
leftovers: Use only properly refrigerated leftovers within the approved label or review window.
servingSuggestions: Serve with rice or as a bibimbap component.

faq.question: Can I gather fernbrake myself?
faq.answer: No. This draft is restricted to commercially identified, fully processed gosari.

faq.question: Can I start with dried gosari?
faq.answer: Not in this conservative checkpoint; dried-product processing needs a qualified safety review.
